meaning: Shaded relief and contour lines derived from a public elevation model. They show the shape of the ground. They do not describe vineyard land, and nothing about slope or height here is evidence for how a wine tastes.

elevation.native_resolution: 1 arc-second grid (3600×3600 samples per 1° tile); ≈30 m north–south and ≈20–23 m east–west across the acquired 42–48°N coverage
elevation.scale_limitations: Usable for regional relief reading down to roughly 1:50,000. It cannot resolve an individual vineyard parcel, a terrace, a wall or a row orientation, and as a surface model it carries tree canopy and building heights as if they were ground.
elevation.uncertainty: The programme specification is LE90 < 4 m vertical and CE90 < 6 m horizontal. The six western-Pyrenean source entries retain their separately checked tile-mask figures; no tile-mask precision beyond the programme specification is asserted for the two Beaujolais, two Loire or one additional Northern Rhône file.

proof_extent.description: Béarn, Jurançon, Pacherenc du Vic-Bilh, Irouléguy and the western Pyrenean front. Outside this bounded extent CARTA Atlas has no terrain.
